long_biography.plain_text:
Edward Lampert's interest in companies began with his grandmother, an enthusiastic stock-market follower who reviewed her picks with him. After his father died when Lampert was fourteen, he worked after school and at weekends while his mother returned to paid employment. Savings from summer jobs helped him pay for an economics degree at Yale.

At Yale, Lampert studied economics and worked as a research assistant for Nobel laureate James Tobin. He later developed a deal-based approach under Robert Rubin, analysing both balance sheets and the motives of managers and shareholders. Those habits became a concentrated investment practice built around a small number of long-held positions.
long_biography.html:
Edward Lampert's interest in companies began with his grandmother, an enthusiastic stock-market follower who reviewed her picks with him. After his father died when Lampert was fourteen, he worked after school and at weekends while his mother returned to paid employment. Savings from summer jobs helped him pay for an economics degree at Yale.

At Yale, Lampert studied economics and worked as a research assistant for Nobel laureate James Tobin. He later developed a deal-based approach under Robert Rubin, analysing both balance sheets and the motives of managers and shareholders. Those habits became a concentrated investment practice built around a small number of long-held positions.
